issues.description: The template Lecture.java declares a constructor with only three parameters (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents), but the problem statement UML and the solution implementation require a constructor with five parameters in this exact order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and lead to compilation/test failures if they do not modify the provided constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the constructor in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java (template) so its signature matches the UML/problem statement and the solution: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors). Alternatively, remove the partial three-parameter constructor and add the correct five-parameter constructor with a TODO body to avoid misleading students.
